settings.title: Settings
settings.themeHelp: The colour theme of the interface.
settings.themeSystemHint: Follows your device's light or dark setting
settings.languageHelp: The language of the interface. Names, dates and places recorded in the tree are shown exactly as they were entered.
settings.treesHelp: Which tree you are looking at, and where each one is kept on this device. Nothing is ever uploaded.
settings.treePeople: {count, plural, =0 {No one yet} one {# person} other {# people}}
settings.treeMoveLabel: New location — full path ending in .json
settings.treeOpenHelp: Point at a tree file you already have — on this disk, an external drive, or a USB stick. It stays where it is.

onboarding.nameTitle: What should we call this tree?
onboarding.nameHelp: A family name usually works — you can change it later.
onboarding.storageHelp: The tree is a single file. You decide where it lives.
onboarding.storagePrivacy: Everything stays on this device. There is no account, no server and no upload — this app never sends your family's data anywhere.
onboarding.storageDefaultHelp: In {dir}, alongside the application. Excluded from version control.
onboarding.storageCustomHelp: An external drive, an encrypted volume, or any folder on this machine.
onboarding.storageResolved: The file will be created at:
onboarding.storageCloudWarning: That folder syncs to the cloud, so a copy will leave this device. Fine as a backup — worth knowing if it wasn't what you meant.
onboarding.preferencesHelp: Both apply straight away, and both are changeable in settings.
onboarding.startTitle: How would you like to begin?
onboarding.startHelp: Either way, you add everyone else from the chart itself.
onboarding.startMeHelp: You go in first, and the chart opens on you. Parents, partners and children hang off that.
onboarding.startEmptyHelp: Add the first person yourself — useful when the tree should begin with an ancestor rather than with you.
onboarding.youHelp: Just enough to put you on the chart. Dates can be vague — “about 1950” is a valid answer.

emptyTree.help: There is nobody in this tree yet. Add the first person and the chart starts from them.
